meta.basis: one square metre of a notional finished masonry wall
meta.notice: All values are fictional demonstration assumptions, not sourced life-cycle inventory or construction specifications.

materials.name: Fired clay brickwork
materials.subtitle: Earth, transformed by heat
materials.description: A familiar masonry system with energy-intensive firing. Durable in many applications, but performance and impacts depend on kiln type, fuel, mortar, and wall design.
materials.note: Example kiln contributes the largest share of the illustrative carbon footprint.

materials.name: Compressed earth block
materials.subtitle: Earth, formed with less heat
materials.description: A conceptual stabilized-earth system that substitutes pressing and curing for high-temperature firing. Binder content and local climate constraints strongly influence real performance.
materials.note: Lower modeled process energy, but a higher fictional water input in this example.

materials.name: Concrete block masonry
materials.subtitle: Aggregates, cement, compression
materials.description: A modular system built from cement-based units. Its embodied impacts are sensitive to cement composition, manufacturing, wall reinforcement, and local procurement.
materials.note: The fictional cement-related manufacturing contribution dominates this example.

materials.name: Reclaimed brickwork
materials.subtitle: Old material, another chapter
materials.description: Previously used bricks recovered for a new wall. Cleaning, selection, breakage, transport, and allocation rules determine whether reuse delivers a lower real footprint.
materials.note: This fictional scenario allocates only recovery and reinstallation burdens to the reused material.

stages.name: The ground remembers.
stages.description: Material begins in a landscape. Clay, sand, stone, and soil are extracted, separated, and prepared. The site itself has a history that does not travel with the finished block.
stages.note: Extraction can alter land, water and habitats; impacts require site-specific evidence.

stages.name: Heat makes an object.
stages.description: Moulding, compression, curing, or kiln firing gives the unit its physical properties. Fuel and process efficiency can dominate the material's embodied emissions.
stages.note: The manufacturing method is material-specific; not every masonry unit is kiln fired.

stages.name: A journey with weight.
stages.description: Units travel from production to storage and finally to a site. Distance matters, but so do vehicle load, fuel, mode, breakage, and repeated handling.
stages.note: Transport kilometres are user-editable scenario inputs in a future data-driven version.

stages.name: A wall is an assembly.
stages.description: Mortar, labour, scaffolding, cutting, material losses and construction choices turn units into a building system. The wall's performance is more than the sum of its blocks.
stages.note: Demo metrics represent a notional wall, not an isolated brick.

stages.name: A life after demolition.
stages.description: A building may be dismantled carefully or demolished rapidly. Some units can be reused, some downcycled, and some discarded. None of those outcomes is automatic.
stages.note: Recovery rates must be measured; avoid assuming every demolished unit can be reused.
